General rules: read AGENTS.md and README.md first. Code, comments, identifiers, commit messages in technical English; match surrounding style. Commit completed stages on your branch. Never read .env or any credential file; never contact the Raspberry Pi (192.168.0.102), the router, or any device from here: deployment is done by the coordinator. Work only inside your owned paths (plus your agents/state file); anything else goes in your report under "coordinator requests". Use RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR: write the failing test first and watch it fail.

Repository: PC-Monitor (read CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md: binding). The dashboard is TypeScript/Vite in ui/ (vite builds into ../src/PCMonitor/wwwroot which is embedded in the .NET exe; do not edit wwwroot). It is shown in a native window (WebView2), in a browser, and inside the MK-PI Homer dashboard overlay. It has just been re-themed (MK cyberpunk look). PROBLEM reported by the owner: there is a lot of wasted empty space - e.g. on a 1920x1080 screen the "MAJOR LOADS" panel's second tile row holds 2 tiles out of 5 and leaves a dead block, "POWER AND COOLING" and "CPU" panels have half-empty rows, and the page is taller than the screen. Owner decision: FIX THE LAYOUT ONLY (no new data, no new panels, no backend changes): tiles should stretch and fill rows, no partially filled rows with dead space, panels in a row equalize height, and big screens should use the width. Mobile layout (360-430 px) must keep working.
A realistic sample of the live /api/snapshot payload (92 KB, from the owner's PC) is at C:/Users/Maciej/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--Github-Repos-pi-homelab/c48ebc90-825c-48b8-a0f9-39849972572e/scratchpad/pcmon-snapshot.json - read it ONLY to learn the shape and sanitize: the committed fixture must not contain real serial numbers, MAC/IP addresses or user names (replace with generic values; hardware model names may be replaced by generic ones too).

THIS TASK (tooling so the layout can be verified without hardware): create ui/mock/ with
 1. snapshot.sample.json - sanitized fixture derived from the real payload (keep its structure and a realistic number of sensors so layouts are representative: CPU with 8 cores, NVIDIA GPU, RAM, 1-2 drives, network adapters, fans).
 2. server.mjs - dependency-free Node (>=22) static+mock server: serves the built UI from ../src/PCMonitor/wwwroot (after "npm --prefix ui run build") and emulates the endpoints the UI uses (/api/snapshot, /api/health, /api/stream as server-sent events with a snapshot immediately and then slowly varying values, /api/settings, /api/diagnostics) by reading ui/src/api.ts, ui/src/types.ts and src/PCMonitor/Server/Api.cs (StreamAsync) for the exact contract; listen on 127.0.0.1 with --port (default 5199).
 3. shots.mjs - runs headless Edge/Chrome (search "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Application\\msedge.exe", Program Files chrome.exe, env BROWSER) against the mock server using --headless=new --timeout=9000 --screenshot (NOT --virtual-time-budget: the SSE stream never goes idle) at 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 1366x768, 1024x768 and 390x844, writing PNGs into --out <dir>.
 4. measure.mjs - the layout metric. It loads the page in headless Chrome/Edge with remote debugging off, using --dump-dom and an injected script (inline <script> appended by a tiny wrapper page that loads the dashboard in an iframe from the mock server, same origin) that, for every grid/flex container that holds tiles or cards, computes: row count, items per row, and for each row the fraction of the container width covered by items (incl. gaps). It prints a JSON report and a per-viewport table and, with --assert, exits non-zero if any non-final-by-design row covers less than 97% of the container width OR any panel pair sharing a row differs in height by more than 2 px OR the document has horizontal overflow. Document in the file header which containers it inspects (derive the selectors from ui/src/styles.css and views/*.ts).
 5. A short ui/mock/README.md. Add NO npm dependencies and do not touch package.json.
TDD: a vitest file ui/src/mock-fixture.test.ts first: the fixture parses and passes the same model/validation functions the UI uses (ui/src/model.ts, types.ts) and contains no IPv4/MAC/serial-looking strings (regex checks). Then the tools. Run node ui/mock/measure.mjs (without --assert) on the CURRENT layout and report the baseline numbers in your report and state file; do NOT change styles in this task.
VALIDATION: npm --prefix ui run typecheck, npm --prefix ui test. Screenshots/measurements are real here (browser exists): include them in your report.
acceptance: ui/mock contains a sanitized fixture, a mock server reproducing the API and SSE contract, a screenshot tool and a measure tool with --assert
mock-fixture.test.ts passes and proves the fixture is valid and sanitized
Baseline layout measurements for the current layout at five viewports are reported
Typecheck and vitest pass; no new dependencies
